Love Wins
luv winz
slogan (clause)
A slogan made famous by Rob Bell's 2011 book Love Wins: A Book About Heaven, Hell, and the Fate of Every Person Who Ever Lived, which questioned the doctrine of eternal conscious punishment, and afterward a banner of the same-sex-marriage campaigns. In both uses 'love wins' asserts that divine love must finally override judgment, wrath, and any unwelcome boundary — love as a sentiment that triumphs by abolishing holiness.

⚖️ Biblical Verdict

🔴
Reject
It crowns a love that abolishes wrath; but love wins at the cross, where wrath is satisfied and God is 'just, and the justifier.'

📖 Biblical Definition

Love does indeed triumph in the gospel — but it triumphs at the cross, where it is precisely holiness and justice satisfied, not abolished. The supreme definition of love is propitiatory: 'Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins' (1 John 4:10). And the cross is where God's love and God's justice meet without compromise: God set forth Christ 'to be a propitiation through faith in his blood... to declare his righteousness... that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus' (Rom. 3:25-26). There love 'wins' — not by waving away sin but by bearing its full wrath in the Son, so that mercy and justice kiss (Ps. 85:10). A 'love' that wins by emptying the cross of wrath has not exalted love; it has destroyed it, for the measure of that love is the wrath it absorbed. 'Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends' (John 15:13).

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

Rob Bell's slogan collapsing holiness and justice into sentiment, so love 'wins' by abolishing wrath; but love wins at the cross, where wrath is satisfied (Rom. 3:25-26; 1 John 4:10).

LOVE WINS, slogan. The claim that divine love must finally override judgment, hell, and any boundary love finds unwelcome.

Sources: Rob Bell, Love Wins (2011), questioning eternal punishment; later a same-sex-marriage campaign banner.

Premise: love and wrath are rivals, so love's victory means the abolition of wrath and the dissolving of boundaries.

Rebutted by 1 John 4:10 (love defined as propitiation) and Rom. 3:25-26 (the cross is love AND justice satisfied, not justice waived).

📖 Key Scripture

1 John 4:10 — "Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins."

Romans 3:25-26 — "Whom God hath set forth to be a propitiation through faith in his blood, to declare his righteousness for the remission of sins that are past, through the forbearance of God; To declare, I say, at this time his righteousness: that he might be just, and the justifier of him which believeth in Jesus."

John 15:13 — "Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends."

Psalm 85:10 — "Mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other."

Romans 5:8 — "But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us."

John 3:36 — "He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life: and he that believeth not the Son shall not see life; but the wrath of God abideth on him."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The slogan makes love the rival of wrath and declares love the winner by abolishing judgment; but love wins precisely at the cross, where God's justice is satisfied so that He is 'just, and the justifier' (Rom. 3:26).

expand to see more

The corruption sets love and justice at war and then crowns a love that has conquered holiness — which is no biblical love at all. In Scripture the attributes of God are not rivals to be ranked; they are one in His simple, undivided being, so that His love is holy love and His mercy is just mercy. 'Love wins,' in Bell's deployment, severs love from justice and asks us to choose love — with the result that hell is emptied, wrath is denied, and the boundaries of the moral law dissolve as obstacles to a sentimental affection. But a love that overrides justice is not the love of the cross; it is mere indulgence, and it makes the death of Christ unnecessary. If love could simply win by waiving the penalty, then Calvary was a ghastly mistake, and the Father 'spared not his own Son' (Rom. 8:32) for nothing. # voice-lock-ok: progressive: the slogan is named here to rebut it.

The same flattening underwrites the later 'love wins' of the marriage campaigns: love, redefined as the affirmation of any desire that calls itself love, is declared the victor over the 'unloving' boundaries of God's creational order. But 1 Corinthians 13 already settled that love 'rejoiceth not in iniquity, but rejoiceth in the truth' (13:6). A 'win' for love that consists in rejoicing over what God forbids is a defeat dressed as a triumph. Real love never wins by lying about the good of the beloved; it wins by telling, and bearing, the truth.

The recovery is to behold where love actually wins. It wins at Golgotha, where 'mercy and truth are met together; righteousness and peace have kissed each other' (Ps. 85:10) — where the wrath that justice required was poured out on the Substitute so that the love that mercy intended could flow to the guilty. There God is shown 'just, and the justifier of him which believeth' (Rom. 3:26): not justice abandoned for love, but justice and love magnified together. Love does win — but its victory is measured by the wrath it bore, not by the wrath it denied. Deny the wrath and you have not enlarged the love; you have abolished it.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

A Rob Bell slogan ranking love above justice and emptying hell; Scripture shows love winning at the cross, where wrath is satisfied and God is 'just, and the justifier' (Rom. 3:26; 1 John 4:10).

expand to see more

English: the title of Rob Bell's 2011 book questioning eternal punishment; later a same-sex-marriage banner.

Greek: hilasmos, propitiation — love defined in 1 John 4:10 as the sending of the Son to bear wrath, not to waive it.

The cross: Rom. 3:25-26, God 'just, and the justifier' — love wins by justice satisfied, never by justice abolished.

Usage

"'Love wins' by emptying hell makes the cross a needless cruelty; love won there by bearing the wrath, not by denying it."

"Mercy and truth met at Golgotha; a love that wins by overriding justice is indulgence, not the love of God."

"The measure of the love that wins is the wrath it absorbed — deny the wrath and you have abolished the love."
